description: Generate one personalized outreach message per people-sheet row and save them as a new prospecting campaign. Takes the exact sheetId of a people sheet. Without rowIds, uses every people row in that sheet (up to 1000, added in batches of 25 within this one call). templateId must be the exact id of a saved template; otherwise the campaign is described inline with name, offering, goal and a concrete cta. goal is the campaign objective; conversion, with a concrete commercial next step in cta, fits a company that sells to businesses and has no campaigns yet. Every sheet column is used as labeled context. Campaign generation does not consume credits. The campaign is saved as a draft; nothing is sent.

businessContext.description: Company/product context used to ground the generated messages.

cadence.description: Optional cadence steps, in the same shape as a campaign cadence update. Omit to generate later.

body.description: Message body for that step. Use {{firstName}}, {{company}}, {{headline}}, {{signal}} and {{senderFirstName}} when writing a campaign-wide template. Leave empty only for a LinkedIn connection request without a note, and for linkedin_like.

branch.description: The path after the LinkedIn invite (only when the cadence has a LinkedIn message after the invite and e-mails or WhatsApp after it): accepted ("Aceitou o convite": the LinkedIn message first, then any steps for who accepted) or not_accepted ("Não aceitou em X dias": e-mails or WhatsApp for who did not accept; X is its first step's day minus the invite's, 1 to 21; never a LinkedIn step). Each person goes down one path. Steps on no path go first, then accepted, then not_accepted. Keep each step's branch as the campaign has it; a cadence sent without branches, with a LinkedIn message waiting for the accept before e-mails, gets the paths by itself.

channel.description: whatsapp_task is a WhatsApp step the person's sender sends from their own phone: a task on the WhatsApp screen, not sent by Nock, only for workspaces that have it (the save refuses it otherwise). linkedin_like is "Curtir post": Nock likes the person's newest LinkedIn post (or recent comment) from the campaign's LinkedIn account, a warm touch before the invite or a message; body empty, no subject; skipped when they posted nothing recent; to have the invite go some hours after the like, give the invite condition no_reply_hours (2 hours is the usual). linkedin_like is an opt-in step, only for workspaces that have it (the save refuses it otherwise).

condition.description: What lets this step go after the one before. no_reply_days (the default): it goes on its day if there is no reply; no_reply_hours: it goes waitHours (1 to 72) after the step before was sent, if there is no reply, and its day is set from that step; invite_accepted: a LinkedIn message right after the invite, after the accept (automatic there); email_opened: only right after an e-mail step, it goes waitHours (default 24, min 1) after the person opens that e-mail and is skipped when it is not opened within fallbackDays (default 5). Opens are approximate (Apple Mail and security scanners). Omit to keep the step's current condition.

day.description: Day in the cadence (1–60). Omit to take the next free slot.

subject.description: Email subject only. Omit for LinkedIn and WhatsApp.

taskDays.description: whatsapp_task only: days the task waits to be sent before the step is skipped (2 when omitted).

constraints.description: Things the copy must never say or do.

cta.description: Desired next step: reply, book_call, accept_connect, share_resource, or custom text such as a demo or trial. Required and specific when goal is conversion.

give.description: Concrete value the sender can deliver before asking for the reader's time.

goal.description: Campaign objective: conversion, awareness, consultative, meeting, relationship, or custom text. conversion fits a workspace with no campaigns yet.

language.description: Defaults to the template language, or "Português (Brasil)".

name.description: Campaign name. Required unless the template supplies one.

offering.description: What the sender offers. Required unless the template supplies it.

rowIds.description: Optional. Exact row ids of that sheet. Omit to use every people row in the sheet (up to 1000).

senderCompany.description: Sender company name used in copy, same as REST senderCompany.

senderCompanyUrl.description: Sender company URL, same as REST senderCompanyUrl.

senderLinkChannels.description: Channels that may include the sender link: email, linkedin, whatsapp.

senderRole.description: Sender role used in copy, same as REST senderRole.

signalGate.description: How to use company buying signals: personalize messages, or skip people missing the chosen signal.

templateId.description: Only the exact id of a saved outreach template. Omit when name and offering are set.

tone.description: Message tone, e.g. consultative, professional, friendly, direct.

whatsappOnly.description: True for a campaign of WhatsApp only (the person picked WhatsApp alone): every step is a WhatsApp their sender sends from their own phone (tasks on the WhatsApp screen; Nock never sends it), no mailbox nor LinkedIn is needed, and only rows with a phone go in. Omit cadence to have it written. Only for workspaces that have the WhatsApp step.

whatsappStep.description: True adds one WhatsApp step near the end of the written cadence that the person's sender sends from their own phone (a task on the WhatsApp screen; Nock never sends it). Only for workspaces that have it; ignored otherwise.
